claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed by the balance between wear-induced passive-film rupture and rapid repassivation.
Increasing Mo and/or Cr concentration in an HEA improves passive-film recovery kinetics.
Improved passive-film recovery concurrently reduces wear damage and corrosion attack.
The proposed baseline is an equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi HEA.
The controlled intervention is to increase Mo and/or Cr content relative to the baseline alloy.
The comparison will use simultaneous sliding wear at fixed load in an acidic electrolyte at elevated temperature.
In situ EIS will be coupled to the tribocorrosion test to monitor passive-film behavior.
A rapidly reforming, stable passive film is the structural mediator that minimizes cumulative wear-corrosion damage.
Mechanical stresses during tribocorrosion repeatedly rupture the passive oxide film.
Enrichment in passivating elements accelerates regrowth of the ruptured passive film.
Faster film regrowth limits the time for which the underlying alloy is exposed to corrosive species.
The modified HEA will have a lower wear rate and reduced volume loss than the baseline under simultaneous wear-corrosion testing.
The modified HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
The modified HEA will recover its open-circuit potential more quickly after wear events than the baseline.
The baseline alloy has less effective repassivation and therefore greater cumulative wear and corrosion.
The predicted benefit should hold at moderate mechanical load and corrosive severity.
The benefit may disappear when wear removes newly formed film faster than it can reform.
The benefit may disappear in an excessively aggressive corrosive environment.
The magnitude and optimum level of the modification depend on composition, competing phases, and test conditions.
Failure of the modified alloy to show statistically significant improvements in wear rate, corrosion current, and passive-film recovery relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
